Jordan: Hey team — Jordan here, first week on runtime. Trying to build from source on Ubuntu 22.04 and hitting a linker undefined reference to cublasLt when linking the runtime. Anyone seen this before?

Ava: welcome! do you know whether you installed CUDA via distro packages or NVIDIA runfile? which driver version?

Jordan: installed CUDA toolkit via apt (nvidia-cuda-toolkit) and drivers from the distro repo. `nvcc --version` shows 12.3, `nvidia-smi` shows driver 515.

Natanael: that mismatch could be it — cublasLt symbols sometimes require newer driver libs. pinging BuildBot for known combos.

BuildBot: CI advisory: our runtime builds against cublasLt symbols present in driver >= 520 when using toolkit 12.x. If driver < toolkit expectation, linker can fail. Recommended: use NVIDIA driver 520+ or build inside container image with matching libs.

Rosie: short checklist: 1) confirm `ls /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcublasLt.so*` 2) check CMake CUDA detection output (it prints detected driver/toolkit paths) 3) try setting `LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/usr/lib/nvidia-520:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH` before build.

Jordan: error snippet: 
```
/usr/bin/ld: /home/jordan/redwood/runtime/build/lib/runtime.a(cublas_ops.o): in function `init_cublas':
cublas_ops.cpp:(.text+0x120): undefined reference to `cublasLtCreate'
collect2: error: ld returned 1 exit status
```

Ava: thanks — that looks exactly like the symbol is missing at link time. Two quick fixes: upgrade the host driver to 520+, or use our dev docker image that bundles matching driver libs. Also in CMake try `-DUSE_CUBLASLT=ON` and verify `-L` flags include the nvidia lib dir.

Natanael: if you want to avoid changing host driver, run: `docker run --gpus all -it --rm -v $PWD:/work redwood/runtime-dev:gpu-520 bash` then `./build.sh` inside container. That mirrors CI.

Jordan: I'll try the docker image now. If that works I'll file a short onboarding note about local driver pitfalls. Thanks folks!

Rosie: welcome aboard — shout if you want a quick pairing sesh. :tada:
